Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

usually adverb

also generally, normally, as a rule, for the most part, be in the habit of, tend to, tend

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam
Cic. Off. 1.135: habentur autem plērumque sermōnēs aut dē domesticīs negōtiīs aut dē rē pūblicā
Traupman 401: usually, plērumque

plērumque

adverb

usually, as a rule, for the most part

In Cicero “as a rule, mostly”; in Tacitus and later often no more than “often” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • soleō, solēre, solitus sum — usually do, be in the habit of

    verb, second conjugation, semi-deponent, with an infinitive · classical · Cic. Off. 3.59: sed hīc piscārī nūllī solent; Ov. Fast. 4.170: quae septem dīcī, sex tamen esse solent

    Latin says “usually” as often with this verb as with an adverb; ut solet, as usual (see as usual).

  • ferē — as a rule, usually; with numbers, about

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 363–364: rūrī ferē sē continēbat; Sen. Ep. 53.1: quae ferē aut in aquam aut in ventum resolvuntur

    Lewis & Short: “in the usual course of things”, as against interdum or rārō; ut ferē fit, as usually happens (Cic. Inv. 2.14).

Examples

  • ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō

    I wake when I like: usually about the first hour, often before, rarely laterPlin. Ep. 9.36.1

  • sed hīc piscārī nūllī solent

    but nobody usually fishes hereCic. Off. 3.59

  • pauper, cui opera vīta erat, rūrī ferē sē continēbat

    being poor, with only his work to live on, he usually kept to the countryTer. Ph. 363–364

See also as usual, always, sometimes, never, practice, used to.
